context.title: UP: Judge who awarded 23 death sentences claims 'injustice' as 97 cases recalled from his court
context.snippet:
A judge questioned the recall of ninety-seven serious criminal cases from his court. He stated that cases with commenced hearings cannot be withdrawn administratively. The judge highlighted that such actions are contrary to established legal procedures. He questioned judicial officers' obligation to comply with unlawful administrative orders. The judge emphasised the importance of judicial independence and responsible power exercise.
The judge said cases in which the hearing has already commenced cannot be withdrawn through an administrative order, without following the procedure laid down by law. Live Events His remarks came in the context of nine administrative orders passed on August 18 by the then Muzaffarnagar district and sessions judge, recalling 97 "part-heard" cases involving serious offences, including murder, from his court. The judge said such cases cannot ordinarily be recalled once their trial or hearing has commenced and described the action as contrary to law and "without jurisdiction". Read more: UP govt seems determined to use Goonda Act as tool of harassment: Allahabad HC He also questioned whether a judicial officer is bound to comply with an administrative direction of a district judge or a sessions judge if the order itself is contrary to law. "If an administrative order passed by a sessions judge or a district judge is contrary to the provisions or directions of law and is, therefore, without jurisdiction, can the officer concerned refuse to comply with it?" the judge asked in the 35-page verdict. He further raised questions about the legal validity of decisions that may subsequently be delivered by a court after cases were shifted under an order that itself was legally invalid. The judge noted that the administrative orders recalling the 97 cases were passed shortly before the then district judge's retirement and, according to reports, the latter did not even give any reason for withdrawing the cases.

§ 24.111 Withdrawal of complaints, objections, and petitions for review; settlement.

(a) At any time prior to the filing of objections to the findings and/or order, a complainant may withdraw his or her complaint under any of the statutes listed in § 24.100(a) by filing a written withdrawal with the Assistant Secretary. - State Regulations
- Compare

(1) Withdrawal of complaint. A complainant may withdraw any part of a complaint prior to notice of a contested case hearing. (a) In the event the administrative law judge designated to conduct the hearing becomes unavailable or withdraws from the adjudication, another administrative law judge may be designated for the purpose of further hearing or issuing a decision on the record as made, or both. At any time administrative law judges deem themselves disqualified, they may withdraw from an adjudication.

(b) Prior to issuance of a decision on the complaint, any party may move that the administrative law judge withdraw on the grounds of personal bias or other disqualification by filing with the administrative law judge an affidavit setting forth in detail the matters alleged to constitute grounds for withdrawal promptly upon discovery of the alleged facts. #### § 1503.623 Withdrawal of complaint or request for hearing.
At any time before or during a hearing, an agency attorney may withdraw a complaint or a respondent may withdraw a request for a hearing without the consent of the ALJ.

Opinion for the Court by Circuit Judge ROGERS.

ROGERS, Circuit Judge.

This is an appeal from the denial of attorneys fees under the Equal Access to Justice Act (“EAJA”), 5 U.S.C. § 504(a)(1). After commencing an administrative civil penalties proceeding, the Federal Aviation Administration (“FAA”) withdrew its complaint and the Administrative Law Judge (“ALJ”) before whom the complaint had been pending dismissed the proceedings with prejudice. Nonetheless, the FAA Administrator ruled that the subject of the complaint was not a “prevailing party” as that term has been interpreted in Buckhannon Bd. & Care Home, Inc. v. West Virginia Dep’t of Health & Human Res., 532 U.S. 598, 121 S.Ct. 1835, 149 L.Ed.2d 855 (2001). Because the dismissal with prejudice has res judicata effect and ended the proceedings, we grant the petition and remand the case to the Administrator to determine whether the filing of the complaint was substantially justified, and if not, to award fees.

I.

On February 6, 2007, the FAA filed a complaint against Green Aviation Management Co., LLC, alleging that on a chartered flight from New Jersey to the Bahamas on December 30, 2005, returning January 2, 2006, its plane carried ten, rather than the approved nine, passengers. ### If we reach a settlement for a STAA complaint during the OSHA investigation, does OSHA need to approve it?

Yes, if a settlement is reached for a Surface Transportation Assistance Act (STAA) complaint during the investigation phase, it must be approved by OSHA. According to 29 CFR 1978.111(d)(1), any settlement agreed upon by the complainant and the employer before findings become final requires the consent of the Assistant Secretary. The Assistant Secretary's approval signifies consent from all three parties and finalizes the settlement.

### How do we settle a STAA retaliation case after it has been appealed to an Administrative Law Judge?

A Surface Transportation Assistance Act (STAA) retaliation case can be settled at any time after objections to OSHA's findings have been filed. According to 29 CFR 1978.111(d)(2), the settlement must be agreed upon by the participating parties and approved by the Administrative Law Judge (ALJ) handling the case. If the case has been accepted for review by the Administrative Review Board (ARB), the settlement must be approved by the ARB instead.

### Can I withdraw my STAA retaliation complaint after filing it with OSHA?

Yes, you can withdraw your Surface Transportation Assistance Act (STAA) retaliation complaint at any time before you file formal objections to the Assistant Secretary's initial findings. You must notify the Assistant Secretary of your withdrawal, either orally or in writing. If the withdrawal is part of a settlement agreement with your employer, that settlement must be submitted for approval as outlined in 29 CFR 1978.111(d).

webiq.title: eCFR :: 14 CFR 406.135 -- Withdrawal of complaint or request for hearing. (FAR 406.135)
webiq.snippet:
eCFR :: 14 CFR 406.135 -- Withdrawal of complaint or request for hearing. (FAR 406.135) ... Title 14 was last amended 5/27/2026. ... § 406.135 Withdrawal of complaint or request for hearing.
At any time before or during a hearing, the complainant may withdraw a complaint or a party may withdraw a request for a hearing without the consent of the administrative law judge. If the complainant withdraws the complaint or a party withdraws the request for a hearing and the answer, the administrative law judge must dismiss the proceedings under this subpart with prejudice.

If an agency attorney withdraws the complaint or a party withdraws the request for a hearing and the answer, the ALJ must dismiss the proceedings under this subpart with prejudice, unless the withdrawing party shows good cause for dismissal without prejudice, except that a party may withdraw a request for hearing without prejudice at any time before a complaint has been filed.
